To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a novel, highly selective, long-acting somatomedin analog with potential therapeutic value in the treatment of growth hormone excess.
the cyclic peptide PTR-3173 was identified as a novel somatostatin receptor ligand that is a potent inhibitor of growth hormone release with negligible effects on insulin and glucagon release.

the novel long-acting SRFI analog PTR-3173 has high affinity to human SRFI receptor subtypes 2, 4, and 5 and is the first selective somatostatine analog for the in vitro and in vivo inhibition of growth hormone release with minimal or no inhibition of glucagon and insulin secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel long-acting SRFI analogs, and we have designed and characterized the most potent and selective somatostanergic analog for the suppression of GH release.
the design of highly selective somatotropes and glucagonostats, which may be used for the treatment of GH- and glucagon-related disorders, respectively.

the discovery of novel, highly potent, and selective somatostatins, which are potential drugs for the treatment of GH-secreting pituitary adenomas, GH-secreting tumors, acromegaly, and GH-dependent gigantism, as well as for the treatment of glucagon-secreting pancreatic tumors and acromegaly.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PTR-317 3 is a novel somatostatin analogue with a high degree of selectivity for the inhibition of GH secretion.

PTR-317- has been identified as the most selective somatostatine analog in the literature, with a 1000-fold selectivity for GH inhibition over glucagon and a 10,000 fold selectivity for GH over insulin.
PTR-3177 is a novel, long-acting SRF analog with high affinity for the human sst5 receptor, and with endocrine selectiveness for GH secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel, long-acting, highly endocrine selective somatostinergic analog, PTR- 3173.

we have developed a new somatostatin-based analog, PTR- 3173, that is highly potent in inhibiting the release of GH, with minimal or negligible effects on the release of insulin or glucagon, respectively.

the integrated approach consisting of molecular modeling of the known agonists, high throughput screening, and receptor binding assays is an efficient tool for the identification of new SRIF analogs, which are more potent and physiologically effective than the clinically used octreotide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of selective SRIF analog is feasible, and the approach used can be employed for the development of other peptide-based drugs.
the integrated approach of combinatorial chemistry and high throughput receptor binding screening can be used for the identification of novel, selective, and potent SRIF analogs.
a rational design of cyclic SRIF agonists can result in a new, highly selective somatotropigenic analog with potential clinical value.
